findings.claim: The floor/ceiling/window background compositor (the OR-blit) is ega.drv DISPATCH ENTRY 15 = FUN_0a93 (file 0xa93..0xbc6). It is a SEPARATE entry from the wall compositor (entry 10 = FUN_1c94 @ 0x1c94). The dispatch thunk table at file 0x3f targets 0xa93 (entry 15). It runs from the relocated transient ega.drv copy at base 0x6ba10 (entry lin 0x6c4a3, plane-0 OR-store at 0x6c541). The function has TWO branches selected by [bp+0x10] (secondIdx): [bp+0x10]==0xffff -> the OR-blit walk (file 0xaa9, the floor/ceiling/window path); else -> an xlatb/palette-remap variant (file 0xbc6). The OR vs plain-copy sub-branch is gated by [bp+0xe] (orFlag): !=0 -> `lodsb; or al,es:[di]; stosb` (merge into the page UNDER the walls); ==0 -> `rep movsb` (plain copy).

evidence.details: Capstone dispatch-header scan: entry 15 thunk @file 0x3f -> 0xa93. Reloc base derived from the page-write-watch cluster: plane-0 OR-store cseip 0x6c541 has +0x14/+0x17/+0x19 plane siblings (file 0xb31/0xb45/0xb5c/0xb75 store offsets) -> base = 0x6c541-0xb31 = 0x6ba10. OR-blit entry 0x6c4a3 fired 168 times over a held-ENTER recompose; ds=es=0x1180 at entry (caller seg; the fn sets ds/es internally from cs:[0x149]/cs:[0x14d]).

findings.claim: THE FORMAT: the background is composited from a list of PLACEMENT records, each placing ONE 4-plane PLANAR sub-image into the off-screen compose page with an OR-merge. There is NO mask byte and NO RLE in the pixel walk — the 'masked-image' name is the OR-MERGE itself (the page is pre-zeroed; the OR-blit ORs background bits in, then the masked WALL writer REPLACES wall pixels on top, so the background shows only where walls are transparent). Per placed image: cx bytes copied per row, w-byte source row stride, planeStride=w*h plane jump, 0x28 dest row stride (one 320px screen row), 0x2000 dest plane stride. The 4 planes are stored CONTIGUOUSLY in the source segment: plane p at srcBase + p*(w*h).

evidence.details: Capstone 0xaf5..0xbc3 (OR branch): per image `mov cl,[bx+3]; [bp-6]=cx (=w, row stride)`; `cl=[bx+4](h); al=[bx+3](w); mul cl; [bp-2]=ax (=w*h, plane stride)`; di=[si+1](destX)+[si+3](bias)+0x28*[si+2](destRow); si=[bx+2](srcOff)+[si+3](bias); ds=cs:[0x149]+[bx](segDelta). Per-row: `mov cx,[bp-4] (=placement [si+4] = COPY WIDTH); push cx (=h, OUTER row count)`. Inner byte loop `lodsb; or al,es:[di]; stosb` cx times for plane 0; planes 1/2/3 do `add di,0x2000/0x4000/0x6000; add si,[bp-2]*p` then the same cx-byte OR-copy. Outer: `pop di; add di,0x28; pop ax; add ax,[bp-6](w); pop si; pop cx; loop` (h rows). Validated: the offline decoder composeBackground() replaying this walk from the captured per-group source segments reproduces the engine background page at 99.93% byte-exact over the OR-written viewport (4458/4461).

findings.claim: The walk is driven by TWO 5-byte-record tables in the placement-walk data segment (ds=cs:[0x149]): (1) PLACEMENT table @cs:[0x190], indexed by the arg [bp+0xc] (placementIdx 0..~360 in the corridor view): {imageIdx(u8 -> image-descriptor table), destX(u8 page byte-col), destRow(u8 page row, *0x28), bias(u8 added to destX-pos AND to srcOff = the sub-tile horizontal crop START), count(u8 = the INNER COPY WIDTH cx in bytes, <= the image's w)}. (2) IMAGE-descriptor table @cs:[0x18e], indexed by placement.imageIdx: {segDelta(u16 added to ds -> source SEGMENT), srcOff(u16 plane-0 source byte offset), w(u8 image width in BYTES per plane row == si row stride), h(u8 image height in rows == outer row count)}. So the floor/ceiling perspective triangle + the geometry-dependent black void (where the corridor opens) + the central portcullis window are ALL encoded as the SET of placement records — per-row/per-column destX/destRow/cx with bias cropping — pointing at a small library of 4-plane planar sub-images. The portcullis WINDOW is the SAME format (small w=4..9 sub-images placed in the x128..192 / y52..143 center), NOT a separate sprite path.

evidence.details: Capstone 0xaa9..0xb1c: `bx=[bp+0xc]; ax=5*bx; si=ax+cs:[0x190]` (placement rec); `es=cs:[0x14d](page seg); ds=cs:[0x149](data seg); al=[si+4]; [bp-4]=ax (cx/count); ax=[si+1]+[si+3](destX+bias); di=ax; al=[si+2]; di+=0x28*al (destRow); al=[si]; bx=5*al+cs:[0x18e]` (image desc); `[bp-6]=[bx+3](w); [bp-2]=[bx+3]*[bx+4](w*h); ax=[bx+2]+[si+3](srcOff+bias); ds+=[bx](segDelta)`. The triangular floor: consecutive 1-row placements with cx widening as the corridor approaches the viewer (e.g. y39 cx12 @x120, y40 cx14 @x104).

findings.claim: CRITICAL GOTCHA (the .snd/wall-atlas class of bug): the OR-blit source segment is a MID-FRAME WORK BUFFER that the engine RE-DECODES per image group (the on-disk compressed floor/ceiling/window asset is decompressed via the standard .pic RLE decoder — maze-texture-decode.json — into this work buffer just before each image's OR-blit). A SETTLED read of a source seg returns garbage: for seg 0x29a3, the at-store bytes (`ab 23 ac ad 6d ad cd 2d ...`) differ from the settled read (`f8 10 00 00 02 70 ...`) in 1437/2048 bytes. So a from-source byte-exact decode MUST snapshot each image's source work buffer AT that image's OR store (capture-on-breakpoint), not from a single settled snapshot. With per-group snapshots the decoder reproduces the background 99.93% byte-exact; with a single settled snapshot it scores ~13% (noise). This matches the wall-compositor finding (maze-stage1-compositor.json source-buffer-redecoded-per-group). The 'asset block' (the 12-byte depth ramp + WROOT header + index table + interleaved-zero blob documented in wmaze-texture-rasterizer.json at far-ptr seg 0x783f) is the ON-DISK / pre-decompression form; the OR-blit consumes the DECOMPRESSED 4-plane planar work buffer, not that block directly.

evidence.details: Capture-on-breakpoint of seg 0x29a3 at the FIRST OR plane-0 store vs a settled read: 1437/2048 bytes differ. Replay parity: settled-snapshot = 13.2% bit-subset; per-group-snapshot = 91.3% bit-subset vs final composed (the rest are wall-overwritten or window timing); per-group + isolated single recompose pass + directly-captured w/planeStride = 99.93% byte-exact (4458/4461) vs the background-only page (the page at the LAST OR plane-0 store, before walls overwrite). Of the bit-subset 'bad' bytes vs the FINAL composed page, 277/391 were wall-overwritten (the masked wall REPLACE writer on top — correct, not an OR-blit error) and only 114 were genuine, all in the window center (the per-group-snapshot timing residual).

findings.claim: The OR-blit (background) runs on a FULL RECOMPOSE (dungeon load + the held-ENTER forward-move recompose), NOT on every per-step wall redraw. A single-frame forward step refreshes ONLY the walls (the masked writer 0x6d9dd) over the PERSISTENT background page; the OR-blit does not re-run. Within one recompose the OR-blit and the wall compositor INTERLEAVE writing the page, but the OR-blit's background bytes are stable until the masked wall writer REPLACES the wall pixels. The held-ENTER forceRedraw runs the recompose ~3 times (each ~566 OR rows / ~8000 plane-0 byte stores); a single pass = ~25 placed images covering the whole viewport (ceiling band, floor band, L/R side panels, the central window strips).

findings.claim: The central portcullis/stained-glass WINDOW is NOT a separate asset/format from the floor/ceiling — it is the SAME OR-blit 4-plane planar format, composited as a cluster of small placement records in the viewport center (x~104..206, y~52..143). The wall compositor (masked REPLACE) also writes the central corridor columns ON TOP, so the final on-screen window is the OR-blit window UNDER the wall faces. No FUN_210c sprite path is involved for the window.

or_blit_walk_pseudocode.per_placement_record: rec @ cs:[0x190] + 5*placementIdx = {imageIdx, destX, destRow, bias, count}; img @ cs:[0x18e] + 5*imageIdx = {segDelta, srcOff, w, h}
or_blit_walk_pseudocode.setup: ds = cs:[0x149] + segDelta; es = cs:[0x14d] (page seg 0x4182); cx(copyWidth) = count; w = img.w (row stride); planeStride = w*h; di = destX + bias + 0x28*destRow; si = srcOff + bias
or_blit_walk_pseudocode.loop: for row in 0..h-1: for p in 0..3: for b in 0..copyWidth-1: page[di + p*0x2000 + b] |= src[si + p*planeStride + b];  si += w; di += 0x28
or_blit_walk_pseudocode.note: copyWidth (count, [bp-4]) is the visible run per row and can be < w (horizontal crop). The vertical/horizontal perspective + black-void come entirely from the SET of placement records, not from per-pixel math. The plain-copy variant ([bp+0xe]==0) uses rep movsb instead of OR (used for opaque chrome).

asm_anchors.name: ega_or_blit_entry15_FUN_0a93
asm_anchors.note: dispatch entry 15 (thunk @0x3f). The floor/ceiling/window background OR-blit. [bp+0xc]=placementIdx, [bp+0xe]=orFlag (1=OR-merge,0=rep movsb), [bp+0x10]=secondIdx (0xffff=OR branch @0xaa9; else xlat branch @0xbc6). Runs relocated (live entry 0x6c4a3, base 0x6ba10).

asm_anchors.name: or_blit_walk
asm_anchors.note: the OR branch: placement+image-descriptor table walk + 4-plane planar OR-copy. Tables at cs:[0x190] (placement, 5B recs) and cs:[0x18e] (image desc, 5B recs); source seg base cs:[0x149], page seg cs:[0x14d].

asm_anchors.name: or_store_plane0
asm_anchors.note: plane-0 inner byte loop `lodsb; or al,es:[di]; stosb` (cx times). Planes 1/2/3 at 0xb41/0xb58/0xb71 (di += 0x2000/0x4000/0x6000; si += p*planeStride). Live plane-0 store = base+0xb31 = 0x6c541.

asm_anchors.name: or_row_setup
asm_anchors.note: per-row entry: ds=source seg, ax=plane-0 src offset, di=dest offset; [bp-6]=w, [bp-4]=copyWidth(cx), [bp-2]=planeStride. Fires once per source row (<4096 ring, single drive captures the whole pass). The trace point used for the live capture is 0xb2c (push cx, cx=copyWidth).

asm_anchors.name: or_blit_xlat_variant
asm_anchors.note: the [bp+0x10]!=0xffff branch: an xlatb (palette-remap LUT @0x192) + dec-si variant of the same planar walk; used for the chrome/recolored placements (orFlag also gates OR vs plain stosb).

asm_anchors.name: ega_drv_reloc_base
asm_anchors.note: the relocated transient ega.drv copy base in CLEAN_STATE (heap-dependent). OR-blit entry = +0xa93 = 0x6c4a3. Wall compositor (FUN_1c94) shares this base. Re-derive per run via the page-write-watch OR-store cluster (plane-0 store has +0x14/+0x17/+0x19 siblings -> base = cseip - 0xb31).

asm_anchors.name: page_to_vram_plane0_store
asm_anchors.note: the offset-preserving page->VRAM rep-movsb (maze-planar-transform.json); used to capture the final composed page (oracle).

caveat_for_prior_findings: CONFIRMS + RESOLVES maze-stage1-compositor.json other-writer-or-blit (the 0x6c5xx ds=0x29c3 OR-blit) and maze-piece-inventory.json's #1-uncracked item: the floor/ceiling/window decoder. The OR-blit is ega.drv DISPATCH ENTRY 15 (FUN_0a93), a 4-plane PLANAR OR-copy driven by placement (cs:[0x190]) + image-descriptor (cs:[0x18e]) 5-byte-record tables — NOT a mask/RLE-walked 'masked-image' (the 'masked' is the OR-merge under the walls). CORRECTS wmaze-texture-rasterizer.json's 'interleaved-zero masked-image blob walked by image_blit': the in-RAM PIXELS are plain 4-plane planar; the interleaved-zero bytes in the floor far-ptr dump are the on-disk COMPRESSED form (decompressed via .pic RLE into the work buffer the OR-blit reads). The 12-byte depth ramp + WROOT header at the floor far-ptr are the heap-block header, not consumed by the OR-blit pixel walk. The source is a per-group work buffer (same class as the wall atlas), which is why every prior settled-read decode of seg 0x29c3/0x783f gave noise.
